sentences: So I look at big(4, 9), and since 4 is less than 9, it prints 9. That printed number goes back to m, so m becomes 9 in the end.
First a equals 4 and b equals 9, and a is smaller so the else branch runs, printing b which is 9. Since that gets handed back to the caller, m is 9.
The function prints whichever number is bigger, which is 9 because 9 is more than 4. That printed 9 returns to m, so I chose m equals 9.
When big is called with 4 and 9, 9 gets printed because it is larger. The value that comes out of the function and gets stored in m is that printed 9.
Looking at the last line, m takes whatever big gives back. Inside big, the bigger number 9 is what gets printed, and that is what comes back to m.
